sections.h2: What are a Streamwood owner's options for selling?
sections.html:
Three doors are open to a Streamwood seller: a broker's listing, a sale you manage alone, or a buyer who pays cash and takes the house untouched. Repairs, renters and the date you need funds usually settle the question.

  • Broker's listing: rewards a house in good order, provided you can sit through inspections and a lender's schedule.
  • Going alone: saves the commission and hands you the pricing, advertising and contract review.
  • Cash, untouched: no buyer repair demands, which suits a worn, inherited or tenant-occupied house.

Rented houses carry a Streamwood-specific wrinkle. The village licenses every rental property, single-family homes and condominium units included, so a landlord who sells should ask what happens to the license at transfer.

sections.h2: Where is Streamwood, and how has the population changed?
sections.html:
Streamwood is a Cook County village in the northwest suburbs of the Chicago area. It belongs to the Tri Village area with Bartlett and Hanover Park, and it was first incorporated on February 9, 1957. The village covers about 7.83 square miles.

The curve was steep, then flat. The census counted 4,821 residents in 1960, 18,176 in 1970, 30,987 in 1990 and 39,858 in 2010. The 2020 count came to 39,577, and the Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 38,277 is 3.3 percent under the 2020 base.

Climate matters for condition. NOAA's 1991 to 2020 normals list a mean January high of 32.3 degrees, a mean July high of 86.9 degrees, 38.02 inches of precipitation and 34 inches of snowfall in a year. Expect inspectors to focus on roofs, gutters and basements.

sections.h2: Which schools, libraries and trains serve Streamwood?
sections.html:
Elgin Area School District U-46, the state's second largest, serves most of the village. A small area east of Barrington Road is served by District 54 for kindergarten through junior high and Township District 211 for high school, and the whole village falls in Elgin Community College District 509.

  • Libraries: the Poplar Creek Library District serves most residents; people east of Barrington Road use the Schaumburg Township District Library, and people west of Route 59 use Gail Borden Public Library in Elgin.
  • Parks: the Streamwood Park District covers most of the village, and the Schaumburg Park District covers the east edge.
  • Rail: the nearest Metra station is in Bartlett, on the Milwaukee District West Line to Chicago Union Station.
  • Bus: Pace Route 554 runs from Streamwood to Schaumburg.

Because boundaries split near Barrington Road and Route 59, tell buyers which district, library and park district apply to your address.

sections.h2: What does the Village of Streamwood require at a sale?
sections.html:
Streamwood has its own real estate transfer stamp, issued by the Finance Department. Its rate is printed as $3.00 per $1,000 of value for each transfer, and three items must reach the village before a stamp is issued.

  • A copy of the deed.
  • A copy of the state's Illinois Real Estate Transfer Declaration.
  • Payment of all outstanding water and sewer charges, including any assessments or penalties owed to the village.

A transfer that changes the deed with no money exchanged needs an exempt stamp instead, priced at $10, and that application requires a signed, notarized deed. Send completed forms to finance@streamwood.org, or call the Finance Department at (630) 736-3810. The closing attorney or title company normally files these, yet the water and sewer clearance is one the seller should expect.

The village's licensing rule for rentals is separate. A single-family or condo rental license costs $155 per building per year, includes the required inspection, and expires December 31. Landlords must finish a free online Crime Free Housing seminar of about an hour before applying.

sections.h2: What does Streamwood's rental program mean for a landlord who is selling?
sections.html:
A landlord should treat the license as part of the house's paperwork, because the village ties renting to inspection and training. Each single-family or condominium rental needs an interior and exterior inspection before the one-year license is issued, and the license must be renewed and paid for every year.

  • The tenant, or the landlord acting for the tenant, signs an inspection consent form before the village schedules the visit.
  • Landlords must show a certificate from the Crime Free Housing seminar, and the village will accept one issued within the last five years by a community in Cook, DuPage, Kane, McHenry or Will County.
  • A sample Crime Free addendum for leases is posted on the village page.

A buyer who plans to keep the tenants should ask for the license record and the latest inspection result. A buyer who wants the house empty will want to know the lease end date before closing. A cash buyer can take a rented house, but the lease still has to be read first.

sections.h2: Who assesses and bills Streamwood property taxes?
sections.html:
The village does not provide property tax services. Assessment is handled by Hanover Township through the Cook County Assessor, and the Cook County Treasurer collects the tax. Current bills are a question for the Treasurer at (312) 443-5100, and past years or delinquent taxes go to the Cook County Clerk at (312) 603-5645.

Cook County reassesses each property once every three years, on a township schedule. The 2026 cycle covered the south and west suburbs, while north suburban townships such as Hanover are reassessed only where something about a property has changed. The Assessor's 2026 calendar still lists Hanover with notices dated October 22, 2026 and a last file date of December 7, 2026 for appeals to the Assessor.

  • Start by looking up your parcel number and notice on the Assessor's website.
  • Find out from the Assessor which exemptions are attached to your parcel.
  • Have your closing attorney explain how the year's bill is divided with the buyer.

sections.h2: What does Cook County require on a Streamwood deed?
sections.html:
Deeds for Streamwood property are recorded by the Cook County Clerk. Its checklist for deeds includes the common address, the Property Index Number, a legal description, mail-to and prepared-by names, grantor and grantee details and a completed MyDec form for the state and county stamps. It also lists the municipality's real estate transfer tax, which is where the Streamwood stamp comes in.

For an exempt transfer, the deed needs exemption language citing 35 ILCS 200/31-45 and Cook County Ordinance 93-O-27, or a grantor and grantee affidavit. Section 31-15 of the Property Tax Code sets the state rate at 50 cents per $500 of value, and your title company can confirm the county amount.

faqs.q: Does Streamwood charge its own transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The village's Finance Department states a rate of $3.00 per $1,000 of value, and it issues the stamp after receiving the deed, the state transfer declaration and proof that water and sewer charges are paid.

faqs.q: Should a landlord keep the Streamwood rental license while selling?
faqs.a: Streamwood requires a license for every rental, at $155 per building per year with an inspection. Keep it in force while the house is rented, and ask your attorney how a tenant's lease passes to the buyer.

faqs.q: Which office assesses a Streamwood home?
faqs.a: Hanover Township does the local assessing through the Cook County Assessor, and the Cook County Treasurer collects the tax. The village itself does not handle assessments or bills.

faqs.q: What happens to water and sewer balances at closing?
faqs.a: Pay them first. The village will not issue the transfer stamp until all outstanding charges, assessments and penalties are cleared.

faqs.q: How many people live in Streamwood?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimated 38,277 residents on July 1, 2025, down from 39,577 counted in April 2020.
